title: Driver Flees Laredo Police Officer After Late-Night Traffic Stop on Del Mar; Nightclub Guard Helps Make Arrest
excerpt: A 44-year-old driver fled on foot after a late-night traffic stop in the 200 block of Del Mar Boulevard on Nov. 15, and a nearby nightclub security guard helped the officer detain him. He faces DWI, evading and resisting charges.
content:
A late-night traffic stop in the 200 block of Del Mar Boulevard turned into a foot chase on Sunday night, Nov. 15, after a 44-year-old driver allegedly resisted detention and ran from a Laredo police officer, according to Hammrod News Laredo TX.

The stop happened at about 9:47 p.m., when an officer spotted a vehicle traveling without its headlights, the report said. The driver was identified as Adrian Ramiro Rocha, 44. During the stop, the officer reported a spilled beer can inside the vehicle and signs of possible intoxication.

Authorities allege that when Rocha was told he would be detained for further investigation, he resisted and fled on foot toward a nearby shopping plaza. The officer pursued him and used force to bring him to the ground, and a security guard from a nearby nightclub helped the officer detain him so the arrest could be completed.

Rocha was arrested and charged with driving while intoxicated, evading arrest, resisting arrest, and driving with an invalid license with a previous conviction or suspension and without financial responsibility, according to the report. Webb County booking records list additional counts, including a second evading count, a second resisting count, and a fraud charge of destroying, removing or concealing a writing. He was booked Monday, Nov. 16, at 7:24 a.m.; bond was set at $3,000 on the second evading charge, $2,000 on the second resisting charge, $2,000 on the DWI charge and $1,000 on the invalid-license charge.

No injuries were reported in the announcement. The charges are allegations, and the case will proceed through the courts.

Source: Hammrod News Laredo TX, Nov. 17, 2026; Webb County booking records, as reported in Webb Watch 956's Nov. 16 police blotter.
